ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=85^\circ$, $\angle B=30^\circ$. Arcs are drawn with radii greater than half of the length of $AB$, centered at points A and B, respectively. The arcs intersect at points M and N, intersect $BC$ at point D. When $AD$ is connected, what is the measure of $\angle CAD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle B=30^\circ$, $\angle C=85^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle BAC=180^\circ-\angle B-\angle C=65^\circ$,\\
From the construction, it is known that $MN$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AB$,\\
hence $DA=DB$,\\
thus $\angle DAB=\angle B=30^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle CAD=\angle BAC-\angle DAB=\boxed{35^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, and AB is the horizontal base; C is at the upper left, and BC slants downward to connect to B, forming triangle ABC. Point D is located on side BC, and segment AD has been connected. There is also a vertical straight line in the figure passing through D and intersecting AB; above this line is labeled N, and below it is labeled M. At M and N there are arc-construction intersection marks, indicating the line MN connecting the intersection points made by arcs of equal radius with A and B as centers. From the figure it can be seen that D is the intersection point of straight line MN and BC. Reasoning: The problem gives ∠B=30° and ∠C=85°, so the sum of the interior angles of the triangle gives ∠BAC=180°−30°−85°=65°. From the construction it can be known that M and N are the intersection points of arcs drawn with A and B as centers and the same radius, therefore straight line MN is the perpendicular bisector of AB. D is on MN, so DA=DB. Thus triangle ADB is an isosceles triangle, and since D is on BC, ∠ABD=∠ABC=30°. From DA=DB, ∠DAB=∠ABD=30°. Therefore ∠CAD=∠BAC−∠DAB=65°−30°=35°.
